findings.text: The recommendation credits the case type with saving 10 client lines, but five come from failure lemmas that the kind-rule proofs can also use. Fix: retain 79 as the historical subtotal and use 74 versus 69 in the recommendation, since Lean accepts the original kind-rule checks with the 10-line `items_taken_outcome` and no `items_aliases`.

The success law still requires `Resolved.cellsReady eval rows = true`, and the client supplies `items_cellsReady` when applying it. Fix: say that `InsertFits` supplies `LiteralData.insertReady` and the successful outcome, while the caller supplies cell readiness and plain subqueries.

The documented `decl_diff.py REV FILE NAME…` invocation cannot reproduce the caller counts because the script expects two revisions and a colon-delimited argument for each declaration. Fix: give the invocation as `python3 decl_diff.py b7854558 94c3fa5e FILE:NAME…`, with one `FILE:NAME` argument per declaration.
The text says an unlisted revision changes code, but `d0c3cb15` changed only the status file. Fix: say that each milestone reports the net code-line change since the preceding milestone.

The status places all 40 lines in the scratch file, but `KindAnyProbe.lean` contains only the 29-line helper and the 11-line client theorem comes from `ItemInsertCaseClaims.lean`. Fix: identify both sources and state that the 11-line proof uses `insert_any_rule` in place of `insert_any_case`.
